chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a will addressed to him: 'Know that the one who strikes Ali with the sword and fights him, if he were entrusted with a sword by him or consulted by him and he accepted that from him, would return the trust to him.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Imam Ali's trustworthiness towards his enemies?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the profound integrity of Imam Ali (AS) by noting that even his adversaries would faithfully execute his trust or offer sincere counsel if consulted, underscoring his universal credibility. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on Ali’s *amanah* (trustworthiness) extending beyond mere loyalty to include the fairness and reliability that compel even enemies to honor him. The narrative serves as a practical model for leadership, where one’s character commands respect and fidelity regardless of political or personal enmity.
